## 1. Purpose / Scope

This ARB submission presents the detailed architecture design for the Provider Self-Service Portal, previously approved at CRB (GW-2026-IN-3847, approved 2026-06-15). The design implements the approved conceptual architecture using Next.js 14, Python FastAPI microservices, Amazon EKS, and PostgreSQL on RDS. This submission seeks final architectural approval and implementation authorization (Gate 3).

- Verify CRB approval and alignment with approved concept (no material deviations)
- Ensure technology choices align with Gainwell Technology Radar (all Green/Adopt)
- Validate C4 Level 3 component architecture for all four bounded contexts
- Confirm CI/CD pipeline design with GitHub Actions and ArgoCD
- Verify HIPAA/MARS-E compliance in detailed security architecture
- Validate risk mitigation for provider adoption and data security
- Review 9-month timeline with resource allocation
- Confirm operational readiness including monitoring, alerting, and DR

### Project Overview

The Provider Self-Service Portal delivers a modern web application enabling Indiana Medicaid providers to manage enrollments, submit claims, track authorizations, and access remittances. The solution was approved at CRB on 2026-06-15 with no conditions. This ARB submission presents the detailed implementation architecture with no material deviations from the approved concept.
page_texts.7:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/arb-good-example.md#solution-architecture-summary]

### Solution Architecture Summary

The architecture uses a Next.js 14 frontend with server-side rendering for performance, deployed on EKS behind CloudFront + ALB. Four Python FastAPI microservices (Enrollment, Claims, Authorization, Finance) implement domain logic using Domain-Driven Design patterns. Async communication via Amazon MSK (Kafka) enables event-driven processing. Data persists in PostgreSQL 16 (RDS Multi-AZ) with Redis (ElastiCache) for caching. Authentication uses Azure AD B2C with SAML federation to Indiana FSSA's Okta IdP.

### Data Architecture

![Data Architecture Model](assets/arb-data-model.svg)

| Data Store | Type | Technology | Capacity Planning | Backup Strategy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider DB | Relational | PostgreSQL 16 (RDS r6g.xlarge) | 500GB initial, 20% annual growth | Automated daily + PITR (35 days) |
| Claims DB | Relational | PostgreSQL 16 (RDS r6g.xlarge) | 1TB initial, 30% annual growth | Automated daily + PITR (35 days) |
| Session/Cache | Key-Value | Redis 7 (ElastiCache r6g.large) | 32GB, TTL-based eviction | Not backed up (ephemeral) |
| Document Store | Object | S3 Standard | 5TB initial (enrollment docs) | Versioning + CRR to DR region |
| Event Store | Append-only | PostgreSQL (events schema) | 200GB, 90-day hot retention | Included in Provider DB backup |

**Data Security & Privacy:**

- Encryption: AES-256-GCM at rest (KMS CMK); TLS 1.3 in transit
- Access Control: Row-level security per tenant; column-level encryption for SSN/DOB/TIN
- PII/PHI Protection: Tokenization for display; full values only on authorized decrypt
- Audit Logging: All data access events to immutable audit table; 7-year retention to Glacier

### Security Architecture

- **Identity Provider:** Azure AD B2C (identity broker)
- **Authentication:** SAML 2.0 federation with IN FSSA Okta; MFA required for all users
- **Authorization:** RBAC with 5 roles (Admin, Biller, Credentialer, Viewer, Auditor)
- **Regulatory:** HIPAA, MARS-E, NIST 800-53 v5 (Moderate)
page_texts.18:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/arb-good-example.md#integration-architecture-details]

### Integration Architecture Details

| Integration Type | Pattern | Technology | Error Handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sync API (provider-facing) | Request-Reply | REST/JSON via API Gateway | Circuit breaker (Resilience4j), retry 3x, fallback cache |
| Async Events (internal) | Pub-Sub | MSK Kafka (3 brokers) | DLQ after 5 retries, manual replay via admin API |
| Batch Files (federal) | Scheduled Transfer | AWS Transfer Family (SFTP) | Checksum validation, auto-retry, email alert on failure |
| Legacy Claims API | Anti-Corruption Layer | REST adapter service | Bulkhead isolation, timeout 30s, fallback to queued submission |

- **API Gateway:** AWS API Gateway with usage plans, throttling (1000 req/s burst), WAF integration
- **API Security:** OAuth2 bearer tokens (JWT), mTLS for service-to-service, API key for external partners
- **API Versioning:** URI versioning (/v1/, /v2/) with 6-month deprecation notice

### Risk Assessment

| Risk ID | Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T-001 | Technical | Claims Engine API v2.1 throughput ceiling (500 req/s) | M | H | Load test at 1000 req/s; async queue fallback; negotiate API upgrade with legacy team | Emily Watson | Monitoring |
| T-002 | Technical | Kafka consumer lag during peak enrollment periods | L | M | Auto-scaling consumer groups; partition increase from 6→12; monitoring alert at 5min lag | Emily Watson | Mitigated |

| S-001 | Security | Session fixation or token replay in provider portal | L | H | Rotating refresh tokens; short-lived access tokens (15min); IP binding; CSP headers | Security Team | Mitigated |
| O-001 | Operation | Provider adoption below 50% in first 3 months | M | H | Incentive program; phased rollout (top-50 providers first); dedicated onboarding team | Angela Rivera | Planned |

page_texts.29:
[resources/work-templates/assets/governance/examples/arb-good-example.md#disaster-recovery--backup]

### Disaster Recovery & Backup

Active-Passive DR to us-west-2 with automated failover for database layer.

| Component | DR Approach | RTO Target | RPO Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Portal Frontend | Multi-AZ (in-region HA) | < 5 min | 0 (stateless) |
| EKS Services | Multi-AZ + standby cluster in DR | < 30 min | 0 (stateless + event replay) |
| PostgreSQL (RDS) | Multi-AZ + cross-region read replica | < 15 min (promote replica) | < 5 min (async replication lag) |
| S3 Documents | Cross-Region Replication (CRR) | 0 (already replicated) | < 15 min |

DR Testing: Semi-annual (full failover test); quarterly (component-level recovery validation).
